quick_english: Then the existence of the circle is briefly described: having established the eastern direction, one stretches the thread uniformly.
Having halved that, one marks again in middle, east, and west; then by half-of-half measure, east and west.
By that much one marks; with thread one gives the twin compass; the fish-joint pair thus becomes in south and north.
In its middle one drops the thread for south-north success; or, with an east-west equal thread, north-south.
One marks from the other mark and from the east too; likewise those are placed in the fish middle, throwing a long thread south-north.
By the measured field's half measure, from the middle one marks toward directions; with two threads arising from two directions, the fish becomes corner-placed.
In the fishes, the Vedas are threads; thus a square is proclaimed, from one onward, as a hundred-ending mandala.
In the Siddhanta tantra, a hundred mandalas are called that seat; what goes in its middle, the chief three mandalas, is remembered.
Middle trident, triple trident, and nine trident are clear; there the trident arrangement is said with infinite divisions.
We say that yoni mandala, shown by the order of true being; in the four-handed Veda-supported form, abandon three parts all around.
Divide all each field by sixteen parts; then the middle of two brahma threads is clearly the brahma place.
Having made a boundary, then the target is the fourth thread from the beginning; then go transversely to the fourth thread thereafter.
In the square, if there are two moons, make the outer half-part; their attached brahma-sutra is situated at the third marman.
If so, in the half of the square, the inward-facing pair would be at the second marman of the hand, immovable.
Having made a pair of full moons, the wise one should turn them from the sixth brahma-sutra point to the third cross part.
Having made a half-square, rotate the thread hanging from the full moon tip, upward-facing, toward the broken-moon pair fire part.
Having abandoned the cross-part pair, from the western broken moon then to the corner, so it would be; make a broken piece with two rotations.
From that one very sharp curved tip a horn is born; the same rule is declared for the second; this rule is clear.
When the middle horn is to be made, in the third upper square and fourth half, an inward-facing pair of moon-halves would be.
And that one full moon, previously turned, should reach as needed; by mutual knot union a bound state arises.
Thus on the second side, from turning the broken-moon pair, the joined cheek-knot should be led forward by the other two middles.
The thread in both sides, by which it becomes sharp and goes to the middle horn, has the second brahma-sutra behind at the bottom of both sides.
With attention it should be grasped by the teacher who knows the ritual; the mantra-knower would be rear-facing in that brahma-sutra.
Having excluded the middle horn, all the previously stated rule then applies to the upward-facing broken-moon pair previously declared.
Then, by two, the gandika well fitted inside, by two front threads, the middle horn pair becomes.
Below, by increase of its part, the lotus has four circles; then the wheel is sixteen-spoked or twelve-spoked, in two ways.
In the middle, the place of Kuleshvari may be space, or tilaka, or lotus, or a six-spoked wheel, or a twelvefold space.
At the trident, seven-spoked, by mere joining from the middle, of lotuses then wheels or spaces, seven becomes.
Mixed or confused by difference of contraction and expansion; then by half-measure of field, one should throw the field there with extra measure.
There the staff is remembered: a part of six-spoked pure essence, very sharp-tipped, red-glowing, causing instant possession.
That goddess Kundalini, called wave and great-wave-possessing, is situated in the kanda called six-cornered and is six-deity-natured.
Spread out and long by eight parts, from half of that; then doors should be made in order by variegated turning.
Forms resting on the Vedas, or merely circular, or with clear horn, one should make, or in reverse order.
Having broken the upward-facing or moon-pair, make four; crooked in the middle, clear downward-facing, situated at the side.
Upright, half-equal, full, joined, and knot-placed; thus the moon's turning is twelvefold and delusion-breaking.
By inward and outward facing, she is again considered twofold; from those divisions of circles there would be countless expansion of divisions.
The mandala's lines vary through the blending of beauty and adornment.
The circles become countless through variations of existence and nonexistence.
Then powders are given according to beauty: vermilion, lapis, and white chalk.
Excellent powders here arise through union of three deities.
All goddesses dance always when they see this circle.
Even without worship, seeing the circle initiates one through the mothers.
The supreme goddess power is established as breath-bearing among the trident rites.
The world is established in this coil through principles and their goddesses.
Three trident-piercing powers sit above as seat, accomplishing enjoyment and liberation.
Therefore one desiring liberation worships this great rite with great splendor.
By merely seeing this circle, spirits, vetalas, and guhyakas flee.
Even one weak in power pleases Shiva directly through worship of this circle.
Always by six months one attains trika knowledge, having obtained and considered by oneself what is to be rejected and accepted.
At the end of the body one becomes Bhairava-self; one desiring siddhi succeeds in this mandala through pervasion and deity placement.
He knows conduct as guru in trika teaching; his foot-dust is to be borne on the head by one desiring Shiva.
Here worship creation, preservation, and destruction in order; the fourth, however, is all-filling from the middle, or in all.
Or perform the four-trident or hidden-staff sacrifice; there worship that fourfold sequence properly and clearly.
Thus this was told in the secret supreme sixfold heart, declared and indicated in Siddhayogishvari-mata.
Having threaded the mandala in front, it grants all desires, equipped with great trident and adorned with lotus wheel.
At each gate draw a trident, excluding the western; or in corners make a great trident with tree.
At the trident tip place trika; thus it is to be made eightfold, or threefold.
Thus the divine city of sky-goers is indicated; it is told in Siddha-tantra teaching, even in another place.
Lotus-born in the middle, with trident peaks by its half; the trident-marked mandala is to be constructed, and lotus-marked in filling.
Now the trident-lotus arrangement is in Shripurva, Trishira-mata, Siddha-tantra, Trikakula, and Devi-yamala-mala.
As stated in the essence treatise, the existence and secrets of tantra are shown clearly, even though the order has been stated before.
In the veda-supported three-hand measure, first divide the eastern half, abandoning all sides, toward east, north, and south.
With three-finger upward slanting eightfold cells, abandon two and two parts, then proceed again south and north.
From Brahma's side, from the fourth living side eastward, a half-part measure gives two moon-segment pairs.
In the third between them, on the south and north sides, in the living principle, the wise one makes a pair of moon segments by inner rotation.
At the farther vital point, reaching the tips of two moon segments, one makes an outward-facing rotation and two moon-segment pairs.
Similarly in Brahma, one does the part and half-part measure, then at the end of the second part on both sides.
Two eastern-going lines are led by wise ones in third-part equality to the tip of the half-moon above, joined to Brahma's thread tip.
One should make two threads for establishing the middle peak; one thread is held in one interval from the living side of that tip.
Bring to the corner end from the corner of the first and second moon segments, and from the farther living side and the corner of the first half-moon.
Just so, lead the thread for establishing two peaks; in the other half of the field there is a staff of two hands, hidden five.
The six-spread four-long measure, with vedic finger below it and impurity essence, has its root below; a sharp tip is desired.
For the first field, make four gates in the directions, measuring a cubit or half, or equal to the breadth.
Outside, make the lotus double; listen, make circles with single-part measures in a veda-like manner.
In the directions eight, and again eight, life threads; sixteen in all, drop the numbered ones in the middle of each pair.
Make the whirling equal to the side life in the third circle, up to this point; then measure the life tip.
Wherever contact is steadied in that connection, the mantra master acts there and leads the leaf tips to success.
In each petal make three and three filaments, double eight fingers to be made, and likewise three horns.
The pericarp is yellow; the filament net is made white, red, and yellow by root, middle, and tip.
The petals are white; with the elephant goad, the seat is likewise four-cornered, half the pericarp, outside.
The feet are white, red, yellow, black from fire in order; four horns, and three circles are intended.
The staff should be blue-red with yellow amala essence; make the red trident as previously appointed.
Behind the gate, in front, leaving four fingers, make the gate veda-cornered, round, mixed, or variegated.
The one-two-three city is equal, joined or both, and variegated with cheek, throat, beauty, adornment, and many decorations.
Thus it is said in the Shridevyayamala: the field has a varied arrangement and is endowed with fine vine-houses, when the veda-supported field exists.
Having made half twelve-fold, horizontally and vertically, the teacher should lower one horizontal portion upward from his own side.
That middle three-part should be rotated at its end; abandoning one portion, one should rotate again in its middle.
From the third part upward, rotating the upward part until the end; from the fourth part upward, but join up and down again.
Rotating upward from that measure, one should appoint by the fourth; the thread joins upward in order up to the brahma-thread.
Having made the portion by order and width, one should diminish it again; the staff is desired as double the half-portion measure.
Taking portion by portion from both ranges, the rotating leaf becomes downward like a pippala leaf.
In the sixteenth part one should draw a lotus; by twelve-angula reduction, above that in the middle portion one should draw the lotus-birth well.
At the end of the middle horn, one should draw the third; likewise here on right and left, one should draw well in the hip lotus.
The pericarp is yellowish; the filament is red, yellow, and white; and the petals placed outside the lotus are white, as counter-obstacle.
The trident is black powder; the brahma-line is white; the trident-tip is joined by flame; and the trident staff is yellowish.
In the middle of the trident, in that lotus, the wise one should always worship the lord; above it the supreme, on the right, and another on the left.
That goddess, beyond supreme time, established as time's end, always devours the trident wheel by mere will.
This power is peace-form and knowledge-form supreme; but foundation is lower, and cessation is both supreme and lower.
The upward-standing Bhairava staff has Sada-Shiva nature; its four powers are gross and subtle in many ways.
This sacrifice is called the Damara three-powered sacrifice; then the trident-lotus rite is described in Trishira.
With principal purifiers such as left nectar, pleasing and purifying, worship the ground, dust, instrument, and chalk from the root.
In a square four-cubit space, place the trident in the middle; it has three hands, fierce form, two cubits, and a large up-down seat pair.
The staff, eight fingers and with three threads, is to be made; at the staff root, the seat is twelve fingers.
Upward from length and height, by four-finger measure; upward from height, four fingers; from length, ten fingers.
Having made the trident-root seat in the middle measured by space-ocean-equal fingers, make the staff a trident divided into three parts all around.
By eight-finger measure all around, the trident tip would be hand-measure; the middle and root become accordingly.
The altar is to be made in the middle; at both sides it is six fingers and twelve fingers long.
From four-finger height at the root, arrange the altar; at both sides it is thus half-moon shaped.
Rotate the chalk thread around the waist, making it two fingers wide and four fingers long by measure, O goddess.
Arrange the left side likewise as the right side, with one finger width from the trident tip in the middle, below and above.
By four-finger measure from width, six fingers from height, then the gaṇḍikā should be made by its own form.
Above the base, O good-vowed one, the trident base should be made; the trident tip should be made one finger, very sharp, six fingers.
The hub middle should be made; below the hub, six fingers, four fingers deep, and the middle should be arranged.
East-west, that trident in the middle; outside that, make with three threads, turning them one by one.
Three lotuses at the trident tip, twelve fingers by Veda parts, in order right, middle, left, with three, eight, and twelve petals.
Three wheels, wind city, an eight-finger lotus called vidyā at the trident base; scatter powder afterward.
Fill the trident up to the staff with rājavarta; on the back of the three threads, three white lines should be.
With white powder at the trident base, the vidyā lotus should be; upward in order, three lotuses are red, red-black, white.
The sky line should be white, one finger thick; leaving that outside, the platform should be made hand measure by measure.
The wall should be square, three times the width from length; then all around, in directions, doors should be hand measure.
Divide the twelve-angula measure gradually into three parts: neck, cheek, beauty, and ornament at the end.
Then make a square wall furnished with lines, using white, red, yellow, and black powders.
Fill the middle with red powders as befits beauty, and follow there what was said earlier about its pervasion.
Night-day division, entry, exit, rotation, pervasion of the anahata place, and the supreme rise of kundali are listed.
The trident goddesses are in the heart place; the trident staff stands at the navel; the trident root is situated in the heart.
Remember the three wheels at the end, lifting repeatedly by kala from the form of the body's middle.
Having traversed the trident staff and trident middle-end ranges, enter root, middle, and end into the shakti abode at the final end.
After making non-pulsation, once turning pulsation and pressing root bliss, one should enter the place of the three shaktis.
There, with effortful worship, all siddhis arise from union of all paths and from sixfold path pervasion.
With effort of all mantra wheels and so on, one should contemplate the trident made of thirty-six tattvas.
At equinox, place the mantras in the supreme mandala; when this is worshipped, one attains the place of the all-lord.
With svastika the fitting rite is to be done; place the channels first, according to muhurta measure.

quick_english: Having made fire vasu-going, destroy moon-located points; in fires and sage middle, destroy up to seat and moon.
It speaks of removing brahman's eye-objects and omitting a small eye among eastward channels in the ocean.
It directs omission in the four corners of the seat from the head and eye triad.
Petals are white, filaments red and yellow, the pericarp gold-like, and leaf tips red.
The sky line is very white, and the seat is endowed with three lines: white, red, and yellow.
Four-colored swastikas lie toward fire and northeast; a coral-like path and weapons are outside.
It describes a sapphire-like thunderbolt, power, lotus-gem radiance, a gold-like staff, and a very red face.
A blue-radiant sword, a calf-shining noose, and a banner adorned with flowers, fruits, and five colors are described.
The mace is gold-like, fierce, and gem-adorned; the trident is blue-lotus-like with a blazing fiery crest.
Above it is a white lotus and a gold-like wheel with radiant beryl-like spokes.
The temple of the god of gods has a very yellow spoke-middle and flame-red outer part, granting all desired fruits.
The trident rite is first performed in a square field of hand measure, divided in three ways.
The middle part is divided in three ways with nine cells, and then this rite is described.
After leaving three middle parts, rotate the thread below so that a crescent-moon shape results.
Rotate from both sides so a shape arises at the tip, then draw the former line there with the thread.
Leaving four fingers by the previous far gate, the wise one destroys the line so a trident shape results.
Leaving half a hand at the trident tip, make lotuses below, with three horns and a lotus with pericarp in the middle of the hand.

Thus this mandala rite has been spoken in concise form by the great teachers.
